symptom: Durable lessons and rejection records existed, but equivalent audits could recur because there was no machine-readable fingerprint gate that had to be consulted before choosing the next attempt.
lesson: Retention is not learning unless the next decision retrieves prior outcomes and changes behavior. Narrative notes alone are insufficient for repeat suppression.
guardrail: Normalize each meaningful attempt into a fingerprint, query append-only learning records before acting, reuse verified success patterns, switch after one unchanged failure, and block a third identical attempt after two unchanged failures.
